user.title: Generic Water Heater Setup
user.description:
Creates a virtual water heater that controls a switch using a temperature sensor.

Modes:
- electric: heats normally using target temperature and tolerances.
- performance: keeps the element on regardless of the target, until the tank's own thermostat stops it.

Smart Eco is controlled with a dedicated select entity and uses the surplus and utility entities below (and an optional template) as the allow/block condition for heating.

Enable Debug Logging to capture detailed decision paths and state transitions in Home Assistant logs.

temperatures.name: Temperatures
temperatures.description: Target step, tolerances and the range the heater may be set to.

cycle_protection.name: Cycle protection
cycle_protection.description: Minimum on and off times, to stop the element short-cycling.

smart_eco.name: Smart Eco
smart_eco.description: The entities and optional template that decide when heating is allowed, and how long a manual override pauses it.

data_description.surplus_entity: An entity that says there is spare power to use, for example a PV-excess binary sensor. While it is active, heating is allowed, and the surplus boost (below) may heat past the normal target.
data_description.surplus_state: The state that means 'active'. 'on' for a binary sensor; for an enum sensor, the state to match. Compared ignoring case.
data_description.utility_entity: An entity that says the utility supply is carrying the house. While it is active and the heater's 'Eco: Use Utility' switch is on, heating is allowed up to the normal target.
data_description.utility_state: The state that means 'active', for example 'on', or 'Utility' for a power-source sensor. Compared ignoring case.
data_description.eco_mode_template_condition: Optional. A boolean template that also allows heating when true, OR'd with the two entities above. Leave empty when the entities say everything. Smart Eco policy itself is controlled by a select entity with modes Off, Off until target reached, On until next manual control, Auto Resume after Delay, and Always ON.
data_description.smart_eco_manual_off_resume_hours: In Smart Eco Mode 'Auto Resume after Delay', manual OFF pauses Smart Eco policy for this many hours before automatic resumption. It is also the bound on 'Off until target reached': if the tank never reaches target, Smart Eco is restored after this long rather than staying down indefinitely.

surplus_boost.name: Surplus boost
surplus_boost.description: Store spare power as heat: while the surplus entity is active and the 'Boost: Use PV Excess' switch is on, heat toward this higher target instead of the normal one.

data_description.surplus_boost_target_temperature: Leave empty for no boost. Not limited by the maximum temperature, which only bounds the target dial. The boost stops at exactly this temperature (the hot tolerance does not apply on top) and starts again below it by the cold tolerance. Heat above the normal target is only ever drawn while surplus is active; on the utility or a battery the heater stops at its normal target. A boost that loses its surplus within 10 minutes of starting is not tried again for 30 minutes, so a heater that eats the very surplus it is chasing does not cycle every few minutes.

fleet.name: Fleet coordination
fleet.description: Stops several heaters stepping on together by spacing their switch-on commands apart. Power balancing itself is not done here.

data_description.fleet_stagger_seconds: Minimum spacing between this heater switching on and any other Generic Water Heater instance switching on. Stops several heaters stepping onto a shared inverter or generator in the same instant when they react to the same trigger. A blocked heater waits and retries; it is never skipped. The largest value set on any instance applies to the whole fleet. 0 disables staggering.

legionella.name: Legionella
legionella.description: Thermal-conditions tracking, and the policy select that runs a disinfection cycle. 'Disinfect' waits for the eco condition; 'Disinfect ASAP' stands Smart Eco down until the tank gets there.

data_description.enable_legionella_sensor: Adds a sensor reporting how favourable this tank's recent temperature history has been to Legionella growth, and how long since it last reached a disinfection temperature. It is a thermal-conditions index computed from ONE sensor at ONE height -- not a measurement of contamination. It cannot see the coldest water in the tank, sediment, biofilm, or any outlet downstream; only a laboratory test can tell you what is in the water. A qualifying cycle is 60 °C held for one continuous hour at the sensor. That threshold is fixed on purpose: below 60 °C a cycle is not a gentler version of the same thing and can leave the tank worse than before.
data_description.legionella_interval_days: How long a completed disinfection cycle counts for before the sensor reports Elevated, and twice that before it reports High. Guidance that prescribes a cycle at all asks for daily in institutional systems; single-family homes are largely outside the scope of those standards, and shipped appliance controllers use anywhere from 3 to 30 days.
data_description.enable_max_temp_history_sensor: Adds a sensor under the same device that tracks the highest recorded temperature over the last 7 days. Disabled by default.

hot_water_in_use.name: Hot water in use
hot_water_in_use.description: Detects a draw from this tank's own temperature falling faster than standing loss allows.

data.enable_hot_water_in_use: Create a Hot Water In Use sensor

data_description.enable_hot_water_in_use: The detector works on this tank's temperature alone; the entity below is optional and only makes it more sensitive.
data_description.water_in_use_entity: A whole-house 'water is flowing' entity. Optional. It corroborates the milder falls that temperature alone cannot settle — it never gates detection, and a steep fall is reported without it.

metering.name: Metering
metering.description: The meter on this heater's circuit, if it has one. Not used for control.

data_description.power_sensor: A sensor measuring what this element draws. Published as the heater's power_sensor attribute, so other integrations (a battery runtime estimate, for instance) can follow the heater's live draw without being configured with the meter themselves.

insights.name: Insights
insights.description: Extra sensors that only report. Switch any off here; saving reloads this heater, no restart.

data_description.enable_element_fault: Turns on when the meter and the relay disagree: drawing while the relay is off, or nothing drawn while it is on and the tank is cold. Needs the power sensor.
data_description.enable_heat_up_rate: Learns how fast this tank warms (C per hour) from its own heating runs, and estimates when it will reach the temperature it is heading for.
data_description.enable_energy_split: Today's element energy in three sensors: while surplus was active, while the utility was, and the rest (battery, generator). An attribution from the Smart Eco inputs, not a measurement. Needs the power sensor.

forecast_preheat.name: Forecast pre-heat
forecast_preheat.description: Store more heat on a sunny day when tomorrow's solar forecast is poor.

data_description.enable_forecast_preheat: While surplus is active and tomorrow's forecast is below the threshold, the surplus boost aims at the pre-heat target instead of the boost target (whichever is higher). Uses surplus only, and the Surplus Boost switch turns it off with the boost.
data_description.forecast_entity: A sensor giving tomorrow's expected production in kWh (Wh and MWh are converted), such as Forecast.Solar's 'Estimated energy production - tomorrow'.
data_description.forecast_min_kwh: Below this, tomorrow counts as poor.
data_description.forecast_preheat_target_temperature: How hot to store the tank on the day before a poor one. Set it above the boost target, or it changes nothing.

data_description.enable_debug_logging: Logs detailed runtime diagnostics, including mode transitions, heating/idle state transitions, threshold decisions, eco condition updates, manual overrides, and switch command/cooldown reasoning. Disabled by default.

error.power_sensor_is_mirror: That sensor is a water heater's own Power (mirror) copy. Choose the meter itself.
error.surplus_boost_needs_surplus_entity: A boost target needs a surplus entity to boost on.
error.heater_already_configured: Another Generic Water Heater already drives this switch. Two heaters on one switch fight over the relay.
error.forecast_preheat_incomplete: Forecast pre-heat needs a forecast sensor, a threshold and a pre-heat target.

shed.name: Shed for load balancing
shed.description: Drop this water heater for load shedding without disturbing user intent. The operation mode and Smart Eco policy are left untouched, so releasing the shed resumes exactly what was configured. Outranks Smart Eco "Always ON". A person asking for heat clears the shed.

release.name: Release load shed
release.description: Release a load shed previously applied with the shed service and resume the operation mode and Smart Eco policy the heater already had. Does nothing if the heater is not shed.

temperature_sensor_unavailable.title: {name}: temperature sensor unavailable
temperature_sensor_unavailable.description: The temperature sensor {entity_id} has reported no reading for more than ten minutes. While it is down the failsafe keeps the heater switched off, so the tank is not heating. The repair clears itself when a reading arrives.

heater_switch_unavailable.title: {name}: heater switch unavailable
heater_switch_unavailable.description: The heater switch {entity_id} has been unavailable for more than ten minutes, so the heater can neither turn the element on nor off, and commands sent meanwhile are lost. The repair clears itself when the switch is back.

disinfection_gave_up.title: {name}: disinfection cycle gave up
disinfection_gave_up.description: A disinfection cycle ran for {days} days without reaching 60 °C for a full hour, so {outcome}. Hold progress reached {progress} minutes. {blocked_by} The repair clears when a new cycle starts or the disinfection policy is changed.
